title_en: Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Issuing the 20th Batch of Guiding Cases
ruling_gist_en:
1. The act of "DNS hijacking," which forces network users to visit designated websites through technical means such as modifying router or browser settings, locking the homepage, or popping up new windows, constitutes the crime of destroying computer information systems. If the consequences are serious, it shall be found to constitute the crime of destroying computer information systems.

full_text_en:
Supreme People's Court

Notice on Publishing the 20th Batch of Guiding Cases

Fa [2018] No. 347

To the High People's Courts of all provinces, autonomous regions, and municipalities directly under the Central Government; the Military Court of the People's Liberation Army; and the Production and Construction Corps Branch of the High People's Court of the Xinjiang Uygur Autonomous Region:

Upon deliberation and decision by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, the following five cases (Guiding Cases No. 102-106), including the case of Fu Xuanhao and Huang Zichao for sabotaging a computer information system, are hereby published as the 20th batch of guiding cases for reference in adjudicating similar cases.

December 25, 2018

Guiding Case No. 102

Fu Xuanhao and Huang Zichao v. — crime of sabotaging a computer information system

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 25, 2018)

Keywords: criminal, crime of sabotaging a computer information system, DNS hijacking, serious consequences, particularly serious consequences

Ruling Gist

1. The act of "DNS hijacking," which forces network users to visit designated websites through technical means such as modifying router or browser settings, locking homepages, or popping up new windows, constitutes sabotage of a computer information system. If the consequences are serious, it constitutes the crime of sabotaging a computer information system.

2. For "DNS hijacking," whether it constitutes "serious consequences" or "particularly serious consequences" shall be determined based on the number of computer information systems that cannot operate normally, the duration of the inability of the relevant computer information systems to operate normally, and the losses or impact caused.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Article 286 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

From the end of 2013 to October 2014, the defendants Fu Xuanhao and Huang Zichao, among others, leased multiple servers, used malicious code to modify the DNS settings of Internet users' routers, thereby causing users to be redirected from navigation websites such as "2345.com" to the navigation website "5w.com" set by them. The defendants Fu Xuanhao and Huang Zichao, among others, then sold the obtained Internet user traffic to Hangzhou Jiushang Technology Co., Ltd. (the owner of the "5w.com" navigation website), with total illegal gains of RMB 754,762.34.

On November 17, 2014, defendant Fu Xuanhao voluntarily surrendered to the public security organ after receiving a phone call from the police. Defendant Huang Zichao voluntarily surrendered. Both defendants truthfully confessed to the above criminal facts after arriving at the case.

The defendants and their defense counsel raised no objections to the charges or the facts.

Judgment

The Pudong New Area People's Court of Shanghai, on May 20, 2015, issued criminal judgment (2015) Pu Xing Chu Zi No. 1460: 1. Defendant Fu Xuanhao was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to three years' imprisonment, suspended for three years. 2. Defendant Huang Zichao was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to three years' imprisonment, suspended for three years. 3. The seized tools of crime and the recovered illegal gains were confiscated and turned over to the state treasury. After the first-instance judgment was pronounced, neither defendant appealed, the prosecutorial authority did not protest, and the judgment has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that, according to Article 286 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China, sabotaging the functions of a computer information system, causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally, with serious consequences, constitutes the crime of sabotaging a computer information system. In this case, the defendants Fu Xuanhao and Huang Zichao committed "DNS hijacking" within traffic hijacking. DNS is an acronym for Domain Name System, which provides domain name resolution services. "DNS hijacking" alters domain name resolution so that access to a specific domain name is redirected from the original IP address to a designated modified IP address, preventing users from accessing the website corresponding to the original IP address or causing them to visit fake websites, thereby achieving purposes such as theft of data or sabotage of the original normal services of the website. The two defendants used malicious code to modify the DNS settings of Internet users' routers, hijacking the traffic of users visiting navigation websites such as "2345.com" to the "5w.com" navigation website set by them, and sold the obtained Internet user traffic. This clearly sabotages the functions of network users' computer information systems, causing the computer information systems to be unable to operate normally, and meets the objective elements of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system.

According to the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Involving Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems, sabotaging a computer information system with illegal gains of RMB 25,000 or more or causing economic losses of RMB 50,000 or more shall be deemed as "particularly serious consequences." In this case, the illegal gains of the two defendants amounted to RMB 754,762.34, constituting "particularly serious consequences."

In summary, the "DNS hijacking" acts carried out by defendants Fu Xuanhao and Huang Zichao violated state regulations by modifying data stored in computer information systems, with particularly serious consequences, and they should be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years according to law. Given that the two defendants, with the help of their families, refunded all illegal gains, did not obtain or disclose citizens' personal information, and both had the circumstance of voluntary surrender with no prior criminal record, they were given a mitigated punishment and granted probation.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Li Jun, Bai Yanli, Zhu Genchu)

Guiding Case No. 103

Xu Qiang v. — crime of sabotaging a computer information system

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 25, 2018)

Keywords: criminal, crime of sabotaging a computer information system, mechanical remote monitoring system

Ruling Gist

An enterprise's mechanical remote monitoring system constitutes a computer information system. Violating state regulations by sabotaging the functions of an enterprise's mechanical remote monitoring system, causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally, with serious consequences, constitutes the crime of sabotaging a computer information system.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Paragraphs 1 and 2 of Article 286 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

To strengthen the management of construction machinery and equipment sold on installment payments, Zoomlion Heavy Industry Science & Technology Co., Ltd. (hereinafter referred to as Zoomlion) put into use the Zoomlion Internet of Things GPS Information Service System. This computer information system consists of the Zoomlion IoT remote monitoring platform, GPS terminals, controllers, and displays. The system has the functions of automatically collecting, processing, storing, transmitting back, displaying data, and automatically controlling equipment. Among them, controllers, GPS terminals, and displays are installed by Zoomlion on each piece of equipment during the manufacturing process. Zoomlion installed the Zoomlion IoT GPS Information Service System on pump trucks sold under "mortgage sales" and explicitly stipulated in the product sales contracts that "if the buyer breaches the contract, the seller has the right to take measures such as stopping or locking the machine" and "until the buyer pays off all the purchase price, the ownership of the product belongs to the seller. Even if the buyer has obtained the motor vehicle registration documents, the ownership of the product still belongs to the seller until the buyer pays off all the purchase price." Then, the remote monitoring and maintenance platform at Zoomlion headquarters monitors the pump trucks. If it discovers situations such as arrears or defaults by customers, it will "lock" the machines through the remote monitoring system. After receiving the "lock" instruction, the pump truck can still start but cannot operate.

In May 2014, defendant Xu Qiang used a "GPS jammer" to unlock five Zoomlion pump trucks owned or managed by Zhong Moumou, Gong Moumou, and Zhang Moumou successively. The specific facts are as follows:

1. Around early April 2014, Zhong Moumou discovered that the pump truck he purchased with license plate Gui A77462 was about to be locked by Zoomlion. He arranged for Xu Moumou to help find someone to unlock it. Xu Moumou then contacted Gong Moumou to inform him about the need to unlock Zhong Moumou's pump truck. After Gong Moumou agreed, he contacted defendant Xu Qiang by phone to unlock the pump truck. On May 18, 2014, defendant Xu Qiang, carrying a "GPS jammer," went with Gong Moumou to Qingzhen City, Guiyang. Defendant Xu Qiang connected the signal wire from the "GPS jammer" to the electric control cabinet on the right side of the pump truck, powered on the "GPS jammer," and successfully unlocked the pump truck with license plate Gui A77462. Afterward, Zhong Moumou paid Gong Moumou RMB 40,000 as an unlocking fee, and Gong Moumou, as agreed, paid RMB 9,600 of that amount to Xu Moumou as an introduction fee. On the same day and the following day, Gong Moumou also brought defendant Xu Qiang to permanently unlock three pump trucks managed by him and owned by his brother-in-law Huang, purchased from Zoomlion and Changsha Zoomlion Used Equipment Sales Co., Ltd. on installment payments, with license plates Xiang AB0375, Xiang AA6985, and Xiang AA6987. Afterward, Gong Moumou paid defendant Xu Qiang a total of RMB 30,000 as unlocking fees for the four pump trucks.

2. In May 2014, Zhang Moumou purchased a pump truck from Zoomlion through a mortgage loan. Due to arrears, Zoomlion locked the pump truck using the IoT system, rendering it unable to operate normally. Zhang Moumou then contacted defendant Xu Qiang by phone to unlock his pump truck. On May 17, 2014, defendant Xu Qiang, carrying a "GPS jammer," went to Xiangyang City, Hubei, and used the same method as above to unlock the pump truck owned by Zhang Moumou with license plate E FE7721. Afterward, Zhang Moumou paid defendant Xu Qiang RMB 15,000 as an unlocking fee.

Upon appraisal, after the GPS terminals of the above-mentioned pump trucks with license plates Gui A77462, Xiang AB0375, Xiang AA6985, and Xiang AA6987 were removed and their control programs were modified, the Zoomlion IoT GPS Information Service System was unable to perform real-time monitoring and remote locking of the pump trucks.

On November 7, 2014, defendant Xu Qiang voluntarily surrendered to the public security organ. During the trial of this court, defendant Xu Qiang refunded illegal gains of RMB 45,000.

Judgment

The Yuelu District People's Court of Changsha, Hunan Province, on December 17, 2015, issued criminal judgment (2015) Yue Xing Chu Zi No. 652: 1. Defendant Xu Qiang was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment. 2. The illegal gains of defendant Xu Qiang, amounting to RMB 45,000, were recovered and turned over to the state treasury. Defendant Xu Qiang appealed. The Changsha Intermediate People's Court of Hunan Province, on August 9, 2016, issued criminal ruling (2016) Xiang 01 Xing Zhong No. 58: rejecting the appeal and upholding the original judgment. The ruling has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Handling Criminal Cases Involving Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems stipulates that "computer information systems" and "computer systems" refer to systems with automatic data processing functions, including computers, network equipment, communication equipment, automation control equipment, etc. In this case, the Zoomlion IoT GPS Information Service System consists of the Zoomlion IoT remote monitoring platform, GPS terminals, controllers, and displays, and possesses the functions of automatically collecting, processing, storing, transmitting back, displaying data, and automatically controlling equipment. This system belongs to communication equipment and automation control equipment with automatic data processing functions and constitutes a computer information system within the meaning of criminal law. Defendant Xu Qiang used a "GPS jammer" to modify and interfere with the Zoomlion IoT GPS Information Service System, causing the system to be unable to perform real-time monitoring and remote locking of the involved pump trucks. This constitutes sabotage of the functions of a computer information system, causing the computer information system to be unable to operate normally, with particularly serious consequences. According to Article 286 of the Criminal Law, defendant Xu Qiang constitutes the crime of sabotaging a computer information system. Xu Qiang voluntarily surrendered after committing the crime and truthfully confessed his crimes, which constitutes voluntary surrender, and his punishment may be mitigated according to law. Xu Qiang refunded all illegal gains and showed repentance, which may be considered for a lenient punishment. Regarding the appeal and defense opinions that "he voluntarily surrendered and refunded all illegal gains, and the first-instance sentence was excessive," upon review, Xu Qiang sabotaged a computer information system with illegal gains of RMB 45,000, resulting in particularly serious consequences, and should be sentenced to fixed-term imprisonment of not less than five years. The first-instance judgment, considering his voluntary surrender and full refund of illegal gains, mitigated his punishment and sentenced him to two years and six months' imprisonment, which is appropriate. The appeal and defense opinions were not adopted. The original judgment had clear facts, sufficient and reliable evidence, correct application of law, appropriate sentencing, and legal trial procedures.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Li Fan, Liu Gang, He Lin)

Guiding Case No. 104

Li Sen, He Limin, Zhang Fengbo, et al. v. — crime of sabotaging a computer information system

(Deliberated and adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court, published on December 25, 2018)

Keywords: criminal, crime of sabotaging a computer information system, interfering with environmental quality monitoring sampling, data distortion, serious consequences

Ruling Gist

An environmental quality monitoring system constitutes a computer information system. Blocking sampling equipment of an environmental quality monitoring station with items such as cotton yarn, thereby interfering with sampling and causing serious distortion of monitoring data, constitutes the crime of sabotaging a computer information system.

Relevant Legal Provisions

Paragraph 1 of Article 286 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts

The Xi'an Chang'an District Ambient Air Automatic Monitoring Station (hereinafter referred to as the Chang'an Sub-Station) was one of 13 national controlled air monitoring stations in Xi'an designated by the Ministry of Environmental Protection (hereinafter referred to as the MEP). It collected and processed monitoring data through an ambient air quality automatic monitoring system and transmitted the data hourly to the China National Environmental Monitoring Centre (hereinafter referred to as the CNEMC). The data was published in real-time on the website and used to compile monthly, quarterly, and annual reports on national ambient air quality, which were released nationwide. The Chang'an Sub-Station was one of two national-level directly managed monitoring sub-stations in the city. Its operation and maintenance were entrusted to Wuhan Yuhong Environmental Protection Industry Co., Ltd. by the CNEMC. Unauthorized personnel other than the maintenance party were not allowed to enter without permission.

On February 4, 2016, the Chang'an Sub-Station was relocated to the rooftop of the Power Building of the Southern Campus of Xi'an University of Posts and Telecommunications in the Chang'an District of Xi'an. Defendant Li Sen took the opportunity of assisting in the relocation of the sub-station to secretly intercept the keys to the sub-station and surreptitiously record the password of the sub-station's monitoring computer. From that time until March 6, 2016, defendants Li Sen and Zhang Fengbo repeatedly entered the Chang'an Sub-Station and used the method of blocking the samplers with cotton yarn to interfere with the data collection function of the ambient air quality automatic monitoring system within the sub-station. Defendant He Limin, knowing of Li Sen's actions, did not stop them but merely required Li Sen to reduce the air pollution values. Defendant Li Sen also repeatedly instructed defendants Zhang Nan and Zhang Xiao to use the same method to interfere with the sub-station's automatic monitoring system, causing multiple anomalies in the sub-station's automatic monitoring data and severe distortion of monitoring data over several time periods, affecting the normal operation of the national ambient air quality automatic monitoring system. To prevent the exposure of their crimes, on March 7 and March 9, 2016, under the instruction of defendant Li Sen, defendants Zhang Nan and Zhang Xiao twice entered the Chang'an Sub-Station to delete the surveillance videos. During February and March 2016, the hourly monitoring data from the Chang'an Sub-Station was transmitted in real-time to the CNEMC, published on the website, and used by the MEP to compile and rank the air quality status of 74 cities nationwide for February, March, and the first quarter of 2016. On March 5, 2016, during routine data review, the CNEMC discovered that the data from the Chang'an Sub-Station was significantly low. Upon inspection, the falsification of monitoring data at the Chang'an Sub-Station was discovered. Subsequently, the public security organs apprehended the five defendants Li Sen, He Limin, Zhang Nan, Zhang Xiao, and Zhang Fengbo. During the trial, defendants Li Sen, Zhang Fengbo, Zhang Nan, and Zhang Xiao all admitted to the charges. Defendant He Limin argued in court that he merely acquiesced to and tolerated Li Sen's act of blocking the samplers and requested to be found not guilty.

Judgment

The Xi'an Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province, on June 15, 2017, issued criminal judgment (2016) Shan 01 Xing Chu Zi No. 233: 1. Defendant Li Sen was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to one year and ten months' imprisonment. 2. Defendant He Limin was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to one year and seven months' imprisonment. 3. Defendant Zhang Fengbo was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to one year and four months' imprisonment. 4. Defendant Zhang Nan was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to one year and three months' imprisonment. 5. Defendant Zhang Xiao was convicted of the crime of sabotaging a computer information system and sentenced to one year and three months' imprisonment. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the defendants appealed, and the judgment has become legally effective.

Reasoning

The effective judgment of the court held that the actions of the five defendants violated state regulations. Article 68 of the Environmental Protection Law of the People's Republic of China prohibits the falsification or alteration of monitoring data or the instruction of others to do so. Article 126 of the Law of the People's Republic of China on the Prevention and Control of Atmospheric Pollution prohibits making false representations in the supervision and management of atmospheric environmental protection. Article 7 of the Regulations of the People's Republic of China on the Security Protection of Computer Information Systems prohibits endangering the security of computer information systems. The five defendants in this case falsified or instructed others to falsify monitoring data by blocking the samplers, making false representations, thereby violating the aforementioned state regulations.

The conduct of the five defendants disrupted computer information systems. Article 11 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Involving Endangering the Security of Computer Information Systems provides that computer information systems and computer systems refer to systems with the function of automatically processing data, including computers, network equipment, communication equipment, automatic control equipment, and the like. According to paragraph 1 of Article 10 of the Interpretation of the Supreme People's Court and the Supreme People's Procuratorate on Several Issues Concerning the Application of Law in Criminal Cases Involving Environmental Pollution, the act of interfering with the sampling of an environmental quality monitoring system, causing serious distortion of monitoring data, constitutes disruption of a computer information system. The Chang'an sub-station is a national-controlled ambient air quality automatic monitoring station. The monitoring data generated by it are transmitted directly to the main monitoring station via system software, published to the public in real time through the government websites of the Ministry of Environmental Protection and the main monitoring station, and used to calculate the ambient air quality index for real-time release. An air sampler is an important component of an ambient air quality monitoring system. PM10 and PM2.5 monitoring data are the two most important indicators in the comprehensive air pollution index assessment. The defendants' acts of blocking the sampling ports of the samplers with cotton gauze or disassembling the samplers inevitably altered the internal airflow field of the samplers, caused distortion of monitoring data, affected the correct assessment of ambient air quality, and constituted interference with the functions of the computer information system, rendering the system unable to operate normally.

The conduct of the five defendants caused serious consequences. (1) Defendants Li Sen, Zhang Fengbo, Zhang Nan, and Zhang Xiao repeatedly blocked or disassembled the samplers, interfering with sampling. Defendant He Limin, knowing of Li Sen's actions, did not stop them but merely required Li Sen to reduce air pollution values. (2) The defendants' interference caused significant anomalies in the monitoring data. Between February and March 2016, the particulate matter monitoring data at the Chang'an sub-station repeatedly showed trends inconsistent with those of surrounding sub-stations. The PM2.5 data at the Chang'an sub-station were abnormal during two periods: from 18:00 on February 24 to 16:00 on February 25, and from 4:00 on March 3 to 19:00 on March 6. The PM10 data were abnormal during three periods: from 18:00 on February 18 to 8:00 on February 19, from 20:00 on February 25 to 8:00 on February 21, and from 19:00 on March 5 to 23:00 on March 6. Specifically, at the Chang'an sub-station, from 19:00 to 22:00 on March 5, 2016, the PM10 data dropped from 361 to 213, a decrease of 41%, while the average of other surrounding sub-stations increased by 14% (from 316 to 361). From 16:00 to 17:00 on March 6, the monitoring value at the Chang'an sub-station rose from 188 to 426, an increase of 127%, while the average of other sub-stations changed little (from 318 to 310). From 17:00 to 19:00 on March 6, the value at the Chang'an sub-station decreased from 426 to 309, a drop of 27%, while the average of other sub-stations changed little (from 310 to 304). Thus, the defendants' acts of blocking the samplers were sufficient to cause severe distortion of monitoring data. The significant distortion of these data was corroborated by the fact that during routine data review, the main monitoring station found that the PM10 data from the Chang'an sub-station were significantly lower than normal. (3) The distorted monitoring data were transmitted in real time to the main monitoring station and published to the public. The hourly average concentration data from the Chang'an sub-station ambient air quality monitoring were released in real time via the internet. (4) The distorted monitoring data were used to compile monthly and quarterly environmental assessment reports. The Ministry of Environmental Protection had relied on these false data in its air quality rankings for the 74 key cities nationwide in February, March, and the first quarter of 2016. These rankings were published and reported to the State Council, affecting the national assessment of air pollution control efforts, damaging government credibility, and misleading environmental decision-making. Accordingly, the defendants' acts of interfering with sampling caused serious consequences, satisfying the element of "serious consequences" under Article 286 of the Criminal Law.

In summary, all five defendants constituted the crime of disrupting computer information systems. Given that all five defendants confessed their guilt after being brought to justice and demonstrated remorse, they may be given lighter sentences in accordance with the law.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Zhang Yanping, Luo Chengxing, Yuan Bing)

Guiding Case No. 105

Hong Xiaoqiang, Hong Liwo, Hong Qingquan, Li Zhirong — crime of operating a gambling establishment

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 25, 2018)

Keywords: criminal / crime of operating a gambling establishment / internet gambling / WeChat group

Ruling Gist:

For the purpose of profit, soliciting gamblers by inviting persons to join a WeChat group, conducting gambling based on the results of competitive game websites, setting gambling rules, using the WeChat group for control and management, and persistently organizing internet gambling activities over a period of time constitute "operating a gambling establishment" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law.

Relevant Legal Provision:

Paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts:

On February 14, 2016, defendants Li Zhirong, Hong Liwo, and Hong Qingquan, together with Hong A and Hong B (both at large), used a rented house near the Valve Base in Yingdu Town, Nan'an City, Fujian Province as a base (later moved to a suite on the fifth floor of Dazhong Electric Appliance City, Huanjiang Road, Yingdu Town, Nan'an City), employed Hong C and others, and used smartphones, computers, and other devices to establish a WeChat group (group nickname: "Xunlong Jue," later changed several times to "(New) Ninety-eight Classmate Chat") to recruit gamblers for internet gambling. Hong A and Hong B, as initiators and investors, were responsible for behind-the-scenes management of the entire group. Defendant Li Zhirong was primarily responsible for finance and maintaining the gambling software. Defendant Hong Liwo was primarily responsible for logistics. Defendant Hong Qingquan was primarily responsible for handling disputes with gamblers. Defendant Hong Xiaoqiang was an investor and introduced gamblers including Chen A to join the WeChat group for gambling. The WeChat gambling group divided start-up capital of RMB 300,000 into 100 capital shares and additionally set 10 technology shares. Among them, defendant Hong Xiaoqiang held 6 capital shares, defendants Hong Liwo and Hong Qingquan each held 4 technology shares, and defendant Li Zhirong held 2 technology shares.

Gamblers joined the WeChat group and transferred gambling funds via WeChat or Alipay to the banker's (nicknames: "Bailong Account Room," "Qinglong Account Room") WeChat or Alipay accounts to be credited as points (one point equal to one yuan). Then, based on the results of competitive game websites such as "PC Egg," they placed bets in the group by betting on high/low, odd/even, etc. The gambling group operated 24 hours a day, with dozens of gamblers per round and daily wagers amounting to hundreds of thousands of yuan. By the time the case was uncovered, the group had accepted a total of RMB 3,237,300 in gambling funds. During its operation, the gambling group distributed dividends twice: defendant Hong Xiaoqiang received RMB 36,000, defendant Li Zhirong received RMB 6,000, defendant Hong Liwo received RMB 12,000, and defendant Hong Qingquan received RMB 12,000.

Judgment:

The Zhanggong District People's Court of Ganzhou City, Jiangxi Province, on March 27, 2017, rendered Criminal Judgment (2016) Gan 0702 Xing Chu No. 367: 1. Defendant Hong Xiaoqiang was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to four years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000. 2. Defendant Hong Liwo was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to four years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000. 3. Defendant Hong Qingquan was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to four years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000. 4. Defendant Li Zhirong was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to four years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 50,000. 5. The illegally obtained proceeds totaling RMB 66,000 surrendered by the four defendants and the six mobile phones, one laptop, and three desktop computer hosts and other items used for the crime and transferred with the case were ordered to be confiscated and turned over to the state treasury. After the judgment was pronounced, none of the four defendants appealed, and the judgment became legally effective.

Reasoning:

The court's effective judgment held that defendants Hong Xiaoqiang, Hong Liwo, Hong Qingquan, and Li Zhirong, for the purpose of profit, solicited gamblers by inviting persons to join a WeChat group, conducted gambling based on the results of competitive game websites by betting on high/low, odd/even, etc., and used the WeChat group for control and management, persistently organizing internet gambling activities over a period of time. This conduct constituted "operating a gambling establishment" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law. Defendants Hong Xiaoqiang, Hong Liwo, Hong Qingquan, and Li Zhirong established and operated a gambling establishment, accepting a total of RMB 3,237,300 in gambling funds, which should be considered "serious circumstances" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law. Their acts all constituted the crime of operating a gambling establishment.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Yang Fei, Song Zhengxin, Cai Hui)

Guiding Case No. 106

Xie Jianjun, Gao Lei, Gao Erqiao, Yang Zebin — crime of operating a gambling establishment

(Adopted by the Judicial Committee of the Supreme People's Court and released on December 25, 2018)

Keywords: criminal / crime of operating a gambling establishment / internet gambling / WeChat group / grabbing red envelopes in WeChat groups

Ruling Gist:

For the purpose of profit, inviting persons to join a WeChat group, using the WeChat group for control and management, conducting gambling by means of grabbing red envelopes, and persistently organizing gambling activities over a period of time constitute "operating a gambling establishment" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law.

Relevant Legal Provision:

Paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law of the People's Republic of China

Basic Facts:

From September 2015 to November 2015, during his activities in the Xiaoshan District of Hangzhou City, Xiang A (already sentenced), together with defendants Xie Jianjun, Gao Lei, Gao Erqiao, and Yang Zebin, for the purpose of profit, invited persons to join a WeChat group established by him and organized them to gamble by grabbing red envelopes in the WeChat group. During this period, defendants Xie Jianjun, Gao Lei, Gao Erqiao, and Yang Zebin each assisted Xiang A by sending red envelopes on his behalf in the gambling red envelope group and received a fee from the rake based on the number of gambling red envelopes sent.

Judgment:

The Xiaoshan District People's Court of Hangzhou City, Zhejiang Province, on November 9, 2016, rendered Criminal Judgment (2016) Zhe 0109 Xing Chu No. 1736: 1. Defendant Xie Jianjun was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to three years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 25,000. 2. Defendant Gao Lei was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to three years and three months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 20,000. 3. Defendant Gao Erqiao was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to three years and three months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 15,000. 4. Defendant Yang Zebin was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to three years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 10,000. 5. The six mobile phones used by the four defendants as tools for the crime and transferred with the case were confiscated and turned over to the state treasury; the criminal proceeds of the four defendants that had not yet been recovered were to be recovered. After the judgment was pronounced, Xie Jianjun, Gao Erqiao, and Yang Zebin appealed to the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province. On December 29, 2016, the Hangzhou Intermediate People's Court of Zhejiang Province rendered Criminal Judgment (2016) Zhe 01 Xing Zhong No. 1143: 1. Affirmed the conviction parts in items 1, 2, 3, and 4 of the Xiaoshan District People's Court's criminal judgment (2016) Zhe 0109 Xing Chu No. 1736 and item 5 on confiscation of tools and recovery of criminal proceeds. 2. Reversed the sentencing parts in items 1, 2, 3, and 4 of the Xiaoshan District People's Court's criminal judgment (2016) Zhe 0109 Xing Chu No. 1736. 3. Appellant (original defendant at trial) Xie Jianjun was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to three years' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 25,000. 4. Original defendant at trial Gao Lei was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 20,000. 5. Appellant (original defendant at trial) Gao Erqiao was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to two years and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 15,000. 6. Appellant (original defendant at trial) Yang Zebin was convicted of the crime of operating a gambling establishment and sentenced to one year and six months' imprisonment and a fine of RMB 10,000.

Reasoning:

The court's effective judgment held that for the purpose of profit, inviting persons to join a WeChat group, using the WeChat group for control and management, conducting gambling by means of grabbing red envelopes, setting gambling rules, and persistently organizing gambling activities over a period of time constitute "operating a gambling establishment" as provided in paragraph 2 of Article 303 of the Criminal Law. Xie Jianjun, Gao Lei, Gao Erqiao, and Yang Zebin, together with others, operated a gambling establishment, and all constituted the crime of operating a gambling establishment, with serious circumstances. Xie Jianjun, Gao Lei, Gao Erqiao, and Yang Zebin played relatively minor roles in the joint crime and were all accomplices. The original judgment erred in failing to find them accomplices, and this was corrected according to law, with a lighter sentence imposed on Xie Jianjun and mitigated sentences imposed on Gao Erqiao, Yang Zebin, and Gao Lei. Yang Zebin voluntarily surrendered after committing the crime and truthfully confessed his criminal conduct, constituting voluntary surrender, and received a lighter sentence according to law. Xie Jianjun, Gao Erqiao, and Gao Lei truthfully confessed their criminal conduct after being brought to justice, and received lighter sentences according to law. Xie Jianjun, Gao Erqiao, Yang Zebin, and Gao Lei returned their illegal gains after the case was uncovered; during the second instance proceedings, Yang Zebin's family also returned illegal gains on his behalf. These circumstances were all taken into account for lighter sentences.

(Judges of the effective judgment: Qian Anding, Hu Rong, Zhang Maoxin)
